headline: Managing Access to the Spirit Sands and Kiche Manitou
reservation: A Manitoba Parks vehicle permit is mandatory and should be purchased online before arrival. Camping at Kiche Manitou Campground requires advance booking through the provincial reservation service, as summer weekends often reach total capacity months in advance.

days.title: Desert Dunes and Spring Pools

stops.name: Spirit Sands
stops.detail: Hike the shifting sand dunes, a unique remnant of the ancient Assiniboine River delta, to see cacti and specialized prairie life.

stops.name: The Devil's Punch Bowl
stops.detail: Visit this stunning turquoise pool formed by an underground stream, creating a lush oasis amidst the dry dunes.

days.driving: Allow 15 to 20 minutes from the park entrance to the Spirit Sands trailhead.
days.note: The dunes can reach high temperatures; it is recommended to complete this circuit before noon.

days.title: Assiniboine River Vistas

stops.name: Steppe Hilland Trail
stops.detail: Climb the ridges for an expansive view of the Assiniboine River valley and its mix of spruce and deciduous forest.

stops.name: Oxbow Woods
stops.detail: Walk through the flood-plain forest to see how the river has changed course over time, creating crescent-shaped lakes.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes for local transfers; most sights are clustered along the main park road.
days.note: River levels fluctuate; check at the visitor center for current conditions if planning to use the boat launches.

days.title: Prairie History and Quiet Hikes
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from the Visitor Centre

stops.name: Epinette Creek
stops.detail: Explore the longer trail systems through spruce forests and open meadows, popular for spotting local wildlife.

stops.name: Seton Centre
stops.detail: Located in nearby Carberry, this site provides context on the naturalist Ernest Thompson Seton who worked in this region.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the return to Brandon, depending on seasonal road work on Highway 5.
days.note: Ticks are prevalent in the tall grass during spring and summer; stay on marked paths.

intel.title: Spirit Sands Capacity
intel.text: The Spirit Sands trailhead has a designated lot that may fill during peak summer weekends. Additional parking is available at the Kiche Manitou day-use area, requiring a short walk or bike ride.

intel.title: Reliability in the Dunes
intel.text: Cell service is generally good in the open prairie sections but becomes spotty in the depressions of the Devil's Punch Bowl. Offline maps are recommended for the Epinette Creek trail system.

intel.title: Glenboro and Carberry Services
intel.text: Fuel and groceries are available in the nearby towns of Glenboro and Carberry. There are no fuel stations within the provincial park itself, so fill up before entering the valley.

intel.title: Seasonal Trail Closures
intel.text: Trail access may be restricted during the spring thaw or following heavy rain due to the sensitive nature of the sandy soil. Check the official Manitoba Parks 'Trail Conditions' page before travel.

intel.title: Highway 5 Connectivity
intel.text: The park is split by the Assiniboine River; ensure you are on the correct side for your intended trailhead as bridge crossings are limited. The main park road is paved, but internal loops are gravel.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Highway 5; stop at the Kiche Manitou entry station to verify your digital permit and collect a paper trail map.
plan.vehicle: Suitable for all vehicles including large RVs in the campground; some secondary trail access roads may be narrow for wide trailers.
plan.goldenHour: The Spirit Sands viewpoints offer the best sunset photography as the low light emphasizes the ripples in the sand dunes.
